articles.title: Newscast - Are The Public Ready To Vote Tory Again? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: We look at whether Kemi Badenoch could lead a Conservative comeback.
articles.body: Today, we look at whether opposition leader Kemi Badenoch can lead a Conservative comeback. Polls have suggested the party’s popularity was at historic lows in 2025 and early 2026, but they’ve been slightly more favourable recently. So, after partygate and Liz Truss’ mini budget, are the British public ready to vote for the party again? We also look at Badenoch’s plans to build 50,000 new prison places in England and Wales, and the government’s rollback on jury trials. You can now listen to Newscast on a smart speaker. articles.title: Jovem convulsiona e cai de escada após votar em Rio Preto | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso ocorreu na manhã deste domingo (4), na Escola Estadual Alberto Andaló em São José do Rio Preto.
articles.summary: Após votar em Rio Preto, jovem de 20 anos convulsiona e cai de escada na Escola Alberto Andaló, sendo socorrido pelo Samu e levado ao hospital.
articles.body:
Jovem convulsiona, cai da escada e é socorrido pelo Samu após votar na Escola Estadual Alberto Andaló, em São José do Rio Preto (SP) — Foto: TV TEM/Desirèe Assis

Um jovem de 20 anos convulsionou, caiu da escada e acabou ferido na boca e no nariz depois de votar na manhã deste domingo (4), na Escola Estadual Alberto Andaló em São José do Rio Preto , interior de São Paulo.

Segundo apurado pelo g1 , ele foi socorrido pelo Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) e levado a um hospital particular. Os policiais militares prestaram apoio no atendimento do jovem.

O rapaz tem histórico de problema de saúde, de acordo com o apurado pelo g1 . O incidente ocorreu na saída da escola, enquanto estava com a mãe. O estado de saúde dele é desconhecido até a última atualização desta reportagem.

A escada que dá acesso a seis seções no local ficou interditada para limpeza por cerca de 30 minutos. Depois a votação seguiu normalmente na escola.

articles.title: Abrigo de Cuiabá tem seção eleitoral para idosos e transforma votação  | G1
articles.standfirst: Mesmo com o voto facultativo após os 70 anos, moradores aptos a votar acompanham debates, escolhem os candidatos e participam das eleições sem sair da instituição.
articles.summary: Mesmo com o voto facultativo após os 70 anos, moradores aptos a votar acompanham debates, escolhem os candidatos e participam das eleições sem sair da instituição.
articles.body:
Conheça os moradores do Abrigo Bom Jesus, local onde possui uma seção eleitoral para que os moradores votem. — Foto: Fernanda Deamo

Pela terceira eleição consecutiva, o Abrigo Bom Jesus, em Cuiabá , recebe uma seção eleitoral para que os moradores possam votar sem deixar a instituição. Dos idosos acolhidos, 39 estão aptos a participar da votação e acompanham o processo eleitoral de perto: assistem aos debates, conversam sobre política e chegam às urnas com o voto já definido.

"Eles são antenados. Grande parte é politizada, conversa sobre política e acompanha os debates. No dia da eleição, torcem pelo seu candidato como qualquer outro eleitor", afirma a diretora do abrigo, Márcia.

Segundo ela, a instalação da seção eleitoral facilita a participação dos idosos, especialmente dos que têm dificuldade de locomoção, e transforma a votação em um momento especial.

"É roupa de festa. Eles se arrumam para votar e vivem esse dia como qualquer brasileiro. Para muitos, manter o título e exercer esse direito fortalece a autoestima e o sentimento de cidadania."

'O voto é a arma mais importante que temos'

Carlos Estevão, 73 anos, o voto é a principal ferramenta de participação do cidadão na democracia e também uma forma de cobrar os representantes eleitos. — Foto: Fernanda Deamo

Um dos moradores orgulhosos em votar é o ex-garimpeiro, Carlos Estevão , 73 anos, que faz questão de acompanhar de perto o período eleitoral e afirma que a escolha do voto exige informação. Morador do Abrigo Bom Jesus há cinco anos, ele diz que acompanha entrevistas, programas de rádio, televisão e jornais para conhecer as propostas dos candidatos antes de decidir em quem votar. Para ele, o voto é a principal ferramenta de participação do cidadão na democracia e também uma forma de cobrar os representantes eleitos.

"Eu estudo bastante. Acompanho rádio, televisão, jornal e revista. Gosto de política porque nada muda se não for pela política. Sempre gostei de ler. Se pudesse, teria mais livros do que uma biblioteca. Informação faz diferença na hora de escolher", afirmou Carlos.

O interesse pelo assunto começou ainda na infância, em Poxoréu, influenciado pela mãe, Honorina Aires Aguiar, que incentivava a leitura mesmo quando o acesso à informação era limitado. Carlos contou que cresceu em uma casa onde revistas e jornais eram compartilhados entre vizinhos e que mantém esse hábito até hoje.

"O voto é a arma mais importante que a gente tem. Depois da eleição, o cidadão tem o direito de cobrar aquilo que foi prometido. Se não for pelo voto, nada muda."

Aos 73 anos, Silvio diz que a participação nas eleições faz parte da sua história. — Foto: Fernanda Deamo

Aos 73 anos, Silvio diz que a participação nas eleições faz parte da sua história. Morador do Abrigo Bom Jesus há pouco mais de dois anos, ele lembra que tirou o título de eleitor aos 18 anos e, desde então, procurou votar em todas as eleições.

Silvio lembra de candidatos em quem votou ao longo da vida e diz que sempre enxergou a eleição como um momento de participação e esperança. Para ele, votar também é uma forma de contribuir com a sociedade.

"Comecei a votar aos 18 anos e votei em tudo. Sempre gostei de votar, para prefeito, presidente e até eleição de bairro. Para mim, votar é uma alegria. É uma distração e uma forma de ajudar o próximo. Quando o candidato da gente ganha, a felicidade é maior ainda", contou.

Mesmo sem acompanhar debates ou noticiários com frequência, ele explica que costuma decidir seu voto a partir da confiança que tem nas pessoas.

"Eu voto por amor à pessoa e para ajudar. Quando os candidatos vêm aqui, a gente conhece um pouco mais deles", afirma.

'Escolher quem nos representa", diz Dairan Pereira, 66 anos

Dairan Pereira, 66 anos, é engenheiro mecânico de formação, bacharel em Direito e apaixonado por literatura, música e tradução. — Foto: Fernanda Deamo

Morador do Abrigo Bom Jesus há cinco anos, Dairan faz questão de continuar participando das eleições por considerar o voto uma das principais formas de representação da população. Engenheiro mecânico de formação, bacharel em Direito e apaixonado por literatura, música e tradução, Dairan afirma que acompanha o cenário político antes de decidir em quem votar. Para ele, acompanhar a política faz parte da vida em sociedade.

"Nós vivemos junto com a política, participando ou elegendo quem vai nos representar. É a forma de escolher quem vai estar lá me representando", afirma.

Dairan também destaca a importância de a Justiça Eleitoral instalar uma seção de votação dentro da instituição de longa permanência. Segundo ele, a medida garante mais conforto e acessibilidade aos moradores, especialmente para aqueles com dificuldade de locomoção. Para ele, essa vivência ajudou a construir a consciência política que mantém até hoje.

"É muito prático. Você imagina uma pessoa cadeirante ou com dificuldade para sair daqui. Ter a urna no abrigo torna tudo mais seguro e confortável. Esses exemplos fizeram parte da minha formação. Eu observava aquilo que considerava positivo e levava para a vida. O voto é muito importante. Poder exercê-lo aqui no abrigo facilita a participação de todos nós e fortalece a cidadania", contou o engenheiro.

Aos 99 anos, Gentil Nicácio guarda na memória décadas de participação nas eleições. — Foto: Fernanda Deamo

Aos 99 anos, Gentil Nicácio guarda na memória décadas de participação nas eleições. Nascido em Tanabi (SP), mudou-se ainda jovem para o Paraná, onde constituiu família, trabalhou como caminhoneiro e tirou o título de eleitor. Há cerca de dez eleições, no entanto, ele deixou de ir às urnas após perder o título de eleitor.

Sobre as eleições na instituição, Gentil afirmou que muitos moradores ainda votam e diz perceber a movimentação de pessoas ligadas às campanhas durante o período eleitoral.

"Eu toda vida votei. Só fiquei uns anos sem votar quando saí da minha terra. Depois tirei o título no Paraná e votei por muitos anos. Se tivesse o título, votaria. Não custa nada apertar o número do candidato", lembra.

Ao fim da entrevista, o assunto saiu da política e foi parar no gato Corintiano, companheiro de Gentil na instituição desde filhote. Quando perguntado, em tom de brincadeira, se o felino também iria às urnas, o caminhoneiro caiu na risada e respondeu: "Não vota, né?".

Gentil Nicácio, de 99 anos, ao lado do inseparável companheiro, o gato Corintiano, durante entrevista sobre sua trajetória e a relação com as eleições. — Foto: Reprodução

articles.title: War on Iran: Is escalation more likely than a deal?
articles.summary: Former Iranian and US diplomats agree that the war on Iran is likely to get worse in the coming weeks.
articles.body:
When US leaders insist that the war on Iran is about nuclear weapons and not about oil, Iran’s leaders don’t believe them, argues former Iranian diplomat Hossein Mousavian.

Mousavian and former US diplomat Alan Eyre – both of whom were involved in previous negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme – tell host Steve Clemons that the conflict is not heading to a peace deal or even a “permanent stalemate” any time soon.

The administration of US President Donald Trump prefers quick wins to diplomacy, argues Eyre, “and the responsibility is on the countries in the region to take more of the lead … with US buy-in, not US leadership”.

articles.title: Erika Hilton recebe ameaça de morte e adia ida às urnas por segurança | G1
articles.standfirst: Deputada federal e candidata à reeleição registrou boletim de ocorrência após receber e-mail com ameaças e ataques transfóbicos; Erika Hilton adiou ida à seção eleitoral para reforçar segurança.
articles.summary: Deputada federal e candidata à reeleição registrou boletim de ocorrência após receber e-mail com ameaças e ataques transfóbicos; Erika Hilton adiou ida à seção eleitoral para reforçar segurança.
articles.body:
Intolerância religiosa contra povos e comunidades tradicionais de matrizes africanas e de terreiros. Dep. Erika Hilton (PSOL - SP) — Foto: Tony Winston/Câmara dos Deputados

A deputada federal e candidata à reeleição Erika Hilton (PSOL) registrou um boletim de ocorrência neste domingo (4) após receber, por e-mail, uma ameaça de morte acompanhada de ataques transfóbicos. A mensagem foi enviada na manhã do primeiro turno das eleições de 2026, quando a parlamentar se preparava para sair de casa para votar.

No e-mail, o autor afirma conhecer dados pessoais e o endereço de Erika e ameaça assassiná-la. “Eu sei tudo sobre você, eu vou te matar em breve”, diz um dos trechos. Em seguida, o remetente afirma que acontecerá um “banho de sangue”. A mensagem também contém insultos transfóbicos contra a deputada.

Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, Erika recebeu a ameaça às 10h26 e adiou sua ida à seção eleitoral para aguardar o reforço de sua segurança pessoal.

A parlamentar solicitou às autoridades a abertura de investigação para identificar o responsável pela mensagem e promover a responsabilização criminal do autor.

A ameaça foi enviada por meio do Onion Mail, serviço voltado a dificultar o rastreamento de mensagens.

O episódio ocorreu no dia do primeiro turno e levou a equipe da deputada a reforçar os cuidados com sua segurança. Erika deve votar ainda neste domingo, acompanhada de sua equipe de proteção.

articles.title: MP aciona Justiça após Zema usar celular na cabine de votação | G1
articles.standfirst: Diretor-geral do TRE-MG afirma, durante entrevista coletiva em Belo Horizonte, neste domingo (4) que ação já foi apresentada ao Tribunal. Caso será analisado pela Corte Eleitoral em data ainda indefinida.
articles.summary: Diretor-geral do TRE-MG afirma, durante entrevista coletiva em Belo Horizonte, neste domingo (4) que ação já foi apresentada ao Tribunal. Caso será analisado pela Corte Eleitoral em data ainda indefinida.
articles.body:
O Ministério Público Eleitoral (MPE) apresentou uma ação à Justiça Eleitoral após o candidato à Presidência da República, Romeu Zema (Novo), usar um celular dentro da cabine de votação em Araxá , no Alto Paranaíba, neste domingo (4).

A informação foi confirmada pelo diretor-geral do TRE-MG, Rodolfo Pacheco , durante coletiva em Belo Horizonte , na tarde deste domingo (4). Segundo ele, o processo já foi protocolado, mas ainda não há previsão para julgamento.

"O Ministério Público ingressou com uma ação em relação a esse fato. Naturalmente, isso ainda vai ser julgado pela Corte. Nós não temos ainda um andamento. Isso não vai ocorrer por agora, mas já foi apresentada pelo Ministério Público Eleitoral uma ação referente a esse fato", afirmou o diretor do TRE-MG Rodolfo Pacheco.

Mais cedo, o presidente do TRE-MG, Carlos Henrique Perpétuo Braga , havia informado que o caso seria apurado pela Justiça Eleitoral e lembrou que o uso de celular na cabine de votação é proibido. Segundo ele, a violação do sigilo do voto pode configurar crime eleitoral.

Questionado sobre o episódio, Zema afirmou que entrou na cabine com o aparelho por hábito e disse que não utilizou o celular durante a votação.

"Eu ando com o celular o dia todo. Ele é quase como se fosse um dedo. Ninguém me lembrou ali e eu fui votar normalmente. Não fotografei nada, não fiz nada com o celular ali. Fui só votar mesmo. A cola eu levei no papel", declarou o candidato.

Com a ação apresentada pelo Ministério Público Eleitoral, o caso passará a ser analisado pelo TRE-MG, que decidirá os próximos encaminhamentos do processo.

Romeu Zema vota com celular na mão em araxá — Foto: Caio Ranieri/TV Integração

articles.summary: Candidata ao Senado por Minas Gerais votou neste domingo (4) na na Escola Estadual Helena Guerra, em Contagem.
articles.body:
A candidata ao Senado Marília Campos (PT) votou em escola estadual no município de Contagem — Foto: Imagem cedida ao g1

A candidata ao Senado por Minas Gerais Marília Campos (PT) votou neste domingo (4) na Escola Estadual Helena Guerra, no bairro Eldorado em Contagem, na Região Metropolitana de Belo Horizonte. Ela chegou ao local de votação por volta de 9h, acompanhada de familiares.

Após votar, Marília falou sobre a sua expectativa quanto ao resultado da eleição.

"Estou confiante, mas a gente lida com toda a imprevisibilidade. Mas [estou] confiante de que o trabalho foi bem feito. Eu visitei muitas regiões, ganhei muita confiança das pessoas. Vamos aguardar, estou com a expectativa a mil", disse.

Marília Campos foi recebida no local de votação sob aplausos e gritos entoando seu nome.

articles.summary: Candidato ao governo do Tocantins votou neste domingo (4), no Colégio Marista na capital.
articles.body:
Ataídes (Novo) vota pela manhã em Palmas — Foto: Ribas Martins/TV Anhanguera

O candidato a governador Ataídes Oliveira (Novo) votou no Colégio Marista, em Palmas, nas primeiras horas da manhã deste domingo (4). Ao chegar ao local, o candidato cumprimentou eleitores e seguiu para exercer a cidadania.

O candidato afirmou que a decisão é do povo e que a vitória vem de Deus.

“Quem mentiu mais parece que teve mais aceitação do povo tocantinense. Isso dói a alma para uma democracia. Nós tentamos levar de uma forma muito reta e direta o nosso plano de governo ao nosso povo, como também chamando a atenção deles. Essa é a nossa mensagem: chamar a atenção, respeitosamente, para a responsabilidade do povo", disse.

articles.title: Resulta eleições no exterior: veja onde Lula e Flávio ganharam | G1
articles.standfirst: Boletins de urna mostram Lula com vitória em mais países, mas o grande colégio eleitoral do Japão coloca Flávio Bolsonaro à frente no total. Veja países com resultados finalizados.
articles.summary: A eleição no exterior mostra Lula vitorioso na maioria das nações, enquanto Flávio Bolsonaro lidera a contagem total de votos impulsionado pelo colégio eleitoral do Japão.
articles.body:
Boletins de urna da Nova Zelândia. — Foto: Lucas Salviano

O g1 realiza um levantamento de boletins de urna em diferentes partes do mundo, apresentando alguns desses resultados com antecedência e checando os dados com o TSE.

Os boletins de urna levantados até agora mostram Lula com vitórias em mais países, mas Flávio Bolsonaro à frente na soma dos votos, graças ao Japão , um dos maiores colégios eleitorais fora do país.

China, Austrália, Arábia Saudita e Finlândia estão entre os países em que Lula venceu. Já Flávio venceu em Japão, Israel, Tailândia e Emirados Árabes.

Ao todo, quase 1 milhão de brasileiros estão aptos a votar no exterior. Há urnas em 186 cidades de 134 países. A maior parte dos eleitores está concentrada em países como Estados Unidos, Portugal e Japão.

articles.summary: Vagas de emprego em Volta Redonda serão preenchidas em mutirão da CBSI nos dias 8 e 9 de outubro nas subprefeituras do Retiro e Santo Agostinho.
articles.body:
A Companhia Brasileira de Serviços de Infraestrutura (CBSI) vai realizar um mutirão de empregos com mais de mil vagas em Volta Redonda (RJ). O processo seletivo vai acontecer nas subprefeituras dos bairros Retiro e Santo Agostinho nos dias 8 e 9 de outubro (quinta e sexta-feira).

Segundo a Companhia, a iniciativa tem como objetivo ampliar o acesso da população às oportunidades de trabalho oferecidas pela empresa.

Ainda de acordo com a organização, para participar, os interessados devem levar o currículo atualizado até as subprefeituras, de 8h às 17h.

Ainda de acordo com a organização, entre as funções estão auxiliar de limpeza industrial, líder de limpeza industrial, auxiliar de logística, motorista de caminhão operacional, montador de andaimes, marteleteiro, operador de equipamentos pesados, encarregado, ajudante de manutenção de estruturas e carpinteiro.

Além de vagas para áreas como mecânica, solda, manutenção, operação de máquinas, elétrica, pintura e serviços gerais.

articles.title: Eleitores em Ribeirão Preto e Franca falam da importância do voto | G1
articles.standfirst: Neste primeiro turno, cerca de 1,8 milhão de pessoas vão às urnas nas 66 cidades da área de cobertura da região de Ribeirão Preto e Franca para escolher seis representantes.
articles.summary: Cerca de 1,8 milhão de eleitores em Ribeirão Preto e Franca participam das eleições e reforçam a importância do voto consciente para o futuro do país.
articles.body:
Eleitores ouvidos pelo g1 neste domingo (4) destacaram a importância do voto . Neste primeiro turno, cerca de 1,8 milhão de pessoas vão às urnas nas 66 cidades da área de cobertura da região de Ribeirão Preto e Franca para escolher seis representantes.

Os votos vão para deputados federal e estadual, dois senadores, governador e presidente.

A cozinheira Isabel Pereira da Silva esteve na Escola Professora Amélia dos Santos Musa, no bairro Ipiranga, em Ribeirão Preto, para registrar o voto. Ela destacou a importância da participação dos eleitores na escolha dos representantes.

“A gente tem que saber escolher, porque tudo está dependendo do nosso voto para o país ir para frente. Todos têm que vir. Quem é mais velho, quem é mais novo, todos têm que participar. Nós temos que ter consciência e votar bem.”

A cozinheira Isabel Pereira da Silva vota na Escola Professora Amélia dos Santos Musa, em Ribeirão Preto, SP — Foto: Érico Andrade/ g1

Para a professora Vanessa Aparecida Mastrogiacomo, exercer o direito ao voto é um passo essencial e que exige responsabilidade por parte da população.

"A gente tem que buscar a melhoria para o nosso país, que está tão complicado. A gente tem que pensar, pesquisar certinho os projetos, tudo o que cada um conseguiu e tentar fazer o melhor", disse.

Aos 17 anos, a estudante Ana Beatriz Mendonça votou pela primeira vez. Ele esteve na Escola Dom Alberto José Gonçalves, no bairro Campos Elíseos, em Ribeirão Preto, com a mãe, Gislaine Lima dos Santos Mendonça. Ana Beatriz destacou a importância da participação dos jovens nas eleições e defendeu o voto consciente.

“Para mim, é muito importante exercer a cidadania e o direito de votar, porque estamos em uma democracia. Votar nulo não é uma boa opção. Temos essa responsabilidade, e votar com consciência também é muito importante.”

A estudante Ana Beatriz Mendonça, de 17 anos, vota pela primeira vez acompanhada da mãe, Gislaine Lima dos Santos Mendonça, em Ribeirão Preto, SP — Foto: Larissa Vieira/ g1

O bispo da Diocese de Franca, Dom Paulo Roberto Beloto, de 69 anos, aproveitou os intervalos entre as missas da manhã para o voto.

"É um momento muito importante. Estamos rezando muito para que o Espírito Santo dê discernimento a todos os cidadãos eleitores, para que possamos escolher representantes que possam cuidar bem do nosso Brasil, das crianças e da educação", afirmou.

O bispo da Diocese de Franca (SP), Dom Paulo Roberto Beloto, aproveitou as primeiras horas da manhã deste domingo (4) para votar — Foto: Igor do Vale/ g1

Sem obrigação de votar, Vitorina Dosvaldo, de 77 anos, esteve na Escola Dom Alberto José Gonçalves, no bairro Campos Elíseos, em Ribeirão Preto, com o marido Décio Dosvaldo, de 84 anos.

Ela afirmou que a principal prioridade ao votar é a busca pela mudança e o desejo de um futuro melhor.

"A minha prioridade de exercer é pela mudança. Mudar o que a gente está vivendo. É isso."

Vitorina Dosvaldo, de 77 anos, e o marido, Décio Dosvaldo, de 84, votam na Escola Dom Alberto José Gonçalves, em Ribeirão Preto, SP — Foto: Larissa Vieira/g1

Quem também não tem mais obrigação de ir às urnas são os aposentados Aldecir Jardim Ribeiro e Flora Célia Ribeiro, ambos de 74 anos. Mas eles fizeram questão de exercer o direito na Escola Estadual David Carneiro Ewbank (CEDE), em Franca.

“Faço questão de votar, não por mim, mas pelos meus netos e bisnetos. É nosso dever escolher e lutar pelas futuras gerações”, disse Aldecir.

Flora afirmou que pretende continuar votando enquanto tiver forças e resumiu sua relação com a urna. “Hoje vejo o voto como a nossa arma para fazer a nossa parte e deixar um legado para os mais jovens”.

Os aposentados Aldecir Jardim Ribeiro e Flora Célia Ribeiro, ambos de 74 anos, votam na Escola Estadual David Carneiro Ewbank, em Franca, SP — Foto: Carolina Ribeiro/ g1

articles.title: Eleitora de 103 anos faz questão de votar e filha a leva em SC | G1
articles.standfirst: Maria Evangelina da Silva Jardim compareceu à urna em Florianópolis com cadeira de rodas. Ela já tinha deixado a 'cola' de votação pronta.
articles.summary: Maria Evangelina da Silva Jardim fez questão de participar, em Florianópolis
articles.body:
Uma eleitora de 103 anos fez questão de votar e apareceu na seção eleitoral de cadeira de rodas, com a ajuda da filha, na manhã deste domingo (4) em Florianópolis . Mesmo sem obrigação legal, por causa da idade, Maria Evangelina da Silva Jardim justificou o esforço: "Gosto de votação".

A eleitora do Colégio Catarinense estava internada até a última sexta-feira (2) para tratar uma infecção urinária. Recém-recuperada, ela foi à urna às 11h.

“São mais de 30 anos cumprindo a minha obrigação de cidadã. Eu vim dar exemplo”, disse.

Por causa da internação, a filha, Adelaide da Silva, contou que não tinha certeza se a mãe votaria neste domingo. Porém, Maria Evangelina já estava com a cola pronta em casa , e a filha quis satisfazer a vontade da mãe.

"Eu disse: 'Como que eu não vou levar minha mãe para votar, se é desejo dela, né?'. Então por essa razão a gente está aqui".

🔎 No Brasil, o voto é obrigatório para pessoas alfabetizadas entre 18 e 70 anos. A partir dessa idade, a votação passa a ser facultativa.

Adelaide ajudou Maria Evangelina levando-a à seção eleitoral e apresentando os documentos para os mesários. Em seguida, auxiliou também na coleta da biometria da mãe e levou a cadeira de rodas à cabine.

O voto da eleitora foi acompanhado também pelo presidente do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de Santa Catarina (TRE-SC), desembargador Carlos Roberto da Silva.

Eleitora de 103 anos aguarda conferência da documentação para votar em Florianópolis — Foto: Reprodução/NSC TV

Mais de 5,7 milhões estão aptos a votar em SC

São 5.725.753 eleitores aptos a votar neste domingo (4) em seções eleitorais espalhadas pelos 295 municípios de Santa Catarina.

A votação começou às 8h e segue até às 17h.

No primeiro turno, o eleitor deverá seguir a seguinte ordem :

Primeiro, vota para deputado federal, com quatro dígitos.

Em seguida, é a vez de votar para deputado estadual ou distrital, no caso do DF, com cinco dígitos.

Na sequência, aparece a tela para votar na primeira vaga para senador (três dígitos).

Assim que a urna computar este voto, o eleitor vota novamente para senador (três dígitos).

Na sequência, escolhe o governador do seu estado (dois dígitos).

E, por fim, vota para presidente da República (dois dígitos).

articles.title: Goiás tem duas prisões e mais de 20 registros de crimes eleitorais | G1
articles.standfirst: Prisões aconteceram em Carmo do Rio Verde e Campos Belos, segundo a presidente do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de Goiás. Até a tarde, houve cinco casos de bocas de urna.
articles.summary: Prisões aconteceram em Carmo do Rio Verde e Campos Belos, segundo a presidente do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de Goiás. Até a tarde, houve cinco casos de bocas de urna.
articles.body:
Delegacia de Carmo do Rio Verde: neste domingo, uma pessoa foi presa por importunação sexual — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

As eleições em Goiás transcorrem normalmente neste domingo (4), mas com a ocorrência de filas em alguns locais de votação, segundo a presidente do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de Goiás (TRE-GO), desembargadora Elizabeth Maria da Silva. Até a tarde, por volta das 15h, duas pessoas haviam sido presas e houve mais de 20 registros de crimes eleitorais.

As prisões, segundo Elizabeth Maria, se referem a um caso de importunação sexual, em Carmo do Rio Verde ; e um por desacato, em Campos Belos .

Em relação aos crimes eleitorais, 23 Termos Circunstanciados de Ocorrência (TCOs) foram lavrados por delegacias. No total, em todo o estado, houve o registro, até o momento, de cinco casos de boca de urna.

Na coletiva de imprensa, a presidente do TRE-GO deu, ainda, um balanço parcial em relação às urnas eletrônicas. Até aquele horário, haviam sido substituídos 35 equipamentos, em todo o estado, após apresentarem problemas diversos. Não houve, porém, impacto nas votações, segundo Elizabeth Maria.

Sobre as filas, a desembargadora afirmou que elas têm ocorrido sem relatos de discussões ou brigas.

"O eleitor goiano entendeu que muitas vezes acontecerão as filas. São seis votos que cada eleitor precisa digitar na urna. Com isso, demanda-se tempo, pela dificuldade de entender todo o manuseio da urna eletrônica", explicou a presidente do TRE.

Todas as seções eleitorais estarão abertas até as 17h deste domingo. Elizabeth Maria garantiu que quem chegar aos locais até esse horário conseguirá votar. "Quem estiver na fila irá receber uma senha e continuará normalmente o processo de votação", detalhou.

articles.title: In 2021, an Indiana content creator and her surgeon husband bought a 1914 schoolhouse; by late 2024, their family moved in and a classroom became their kitchen
articles.summary: Discover how Stacie Grissom and her husband transformed a historic 1914 schoolhouse in Indiana into a modern family home while preserving its educational heritage. This renovation story showcases creative preservation and adaptive reuse.
articles.body: A structural restoration in Franklin, Indiana, has completely transformed a historic schoolhouse from the 1910s into a modern residential estate. Houseowner Stacie Grissom and her husband, Sean Wilson, an orthopedic surgeon, became owners of the 9,000-square-foot landmark structure for $175,000 in August 2021 and completed their residential relocation by late 2024 as reported by CNBC.Originally constructed in 1914, the property holds a historical sentiment in the local community. As per CNBC, the building went by the name Union Joint Graded School No. 9 owing to the fact that it admitted children living across the outer boundaries of two adjacent school districts. The facility, until 1934, operated as an active school, after which it was converted into a barn housing pigs, chickens, sheep, and cattle till the mid-1950s. At that point, a former student became the owner, turned it into a private family residence, and remained the custodian until Grissom bought it.The structural overhaul brought major problemsThe initial phase of the reconstruction was met with the challenge of dense paver bricks used in road construction, which made wall removal difficult. Though the masonry remained intact, roof neglect for decades had resulted in extensive water damage. “We had to take down all of the walls and things that had been built by the previous owner,” Grissom told Bernabeo.The massive spatial scale of the building, characterized by 13-foot ceilings and 96-inch-tall windows, also brought challenges to professional contractors, who would arrive, see the massive space, and immediately turn it down. To counter the staffing issue, Grissom's father, a veteran in the construction industry, stepped in and secured a commercial construction crew that treated the restoration as a "cute, weird little project.”Despite its changing uses over the decades, Grissom said the building was never truly abandoned and had long been loved by members of the community. The restoration also uncovered traces of its educational past, including a 1917 teacher’s guide designed for rural students. These discoveries added another layer to the renovation, allowing the family to retain the building’s historical character while adapting its spaces for contemporary family life.The schoolhouse became a family home The finalized layout accommodates four bedrooms, two and a half bathrooms and a kitchen inside what was once a classroom on the upper level, which the family occupies. Concurrently, the lower sub-basement level is still under construction and is being turned into a private guest quarters, a custom workshop and a children's playroom nicknamed "the dungeon".In order to preserve the building's integrity, original color schemes of the school have been used along with installed hand-built mosaic entryways and curated authentic vintage schoolhouse furniture, CNBC noted. Grissom's other structural plans are to eventually turn part of the basement into an indoor playground with swings and a small skating rink.The family has pivoted away from their initial homesteading plans and outdoor strategy and now set sights on building a native landscape of food forest and wildflower meadow. Grissom's chronicle of the overhaul has garnered a massive following, though she was far from a novice when it came to digital storytelling. Her social channels gained huge traction, amassing nearly one million followers on Instagram and roughly 500,000 YouTube subscribers. The project is an example of adaptive reuse, a preservation approach in which an existing building is given a new function rather than being replaced, and Grissom said the schoolhouse would not be useful if it had been preserved only as a school.You use AI every day. articles.title: Japan summons US envoy as marine arrested over Okinawa murder
articles.summary: Ambassador vows cooperation as Japan protests after a US marine’s arrest in connection to Okinawa murder case.
articles.body:
Japan has summoned the United States envoy after a US marine was arrested on suspicion of robbing and murdering a woman.

US ambassador to Japan George Glass pledged “full cooperation” on Sunday. Lance-Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard is accused of killing 39-year-old Anna Yagi on the southern island of Okinawa, where thousands of US servicemen are stationed.

“The occurrence of such an extremely brutal and heinous incident is a matter of profound regret,” Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi wrote on social media. “As the Government of Japan, we have lodged a strong protest with the US side, while firmly demanding maximum cooperation with the investigation.”

Glass stated that the US “confirmed our policy of providing full cooperation with the investigation” while sharing his condolences on social media. The 20-year-old marine has denied the charges.

CCTV footage, according to local Japanese media, showed a non-Japanese man going into a hotel room with the Japanese woman in the city of Naha. Later on, the footage shows the man leaving by himself, with what appear to be the woman’s belongings, reports the AFP news agency.

“Incidents and accidents involving US military personnel cause significant anxiety to the local community and must never occur,” Japan’s Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi wrote on social media.

Japan hosts about 54,000 US military personnel, including 18,000 marines. The majority of these forces are based in Okinawa, a Japanese island that came under US administrative control at the end of World War II and was returned to Japan in 1972.

Since the handover, about 6,000 US military personnel have been arrested in Japan, according to the local newspaper Yomiuri Shimbun.

articles.title: Cornell sexual assault case: Woman at centre of rape allegations got threats to withdraw lawsuit, lawyer says
articles.summary: A woman who has alleged that she was drugged and raped by several Cornell University fraternity members has been threatened with harm if she does not
articles.body: A woman who has alleged that she was drugged and raped by several Cornell University fraternity members has been threatened with harm if she does not withdraw her civil lawsuit, her lawyer said on Sunday.Thomas Giuffra, who represents the woman identified as "Jane Doe", told CNN that she had received multiple threats aimed at forcing her to drop the lawsuit, which alleges that several members of the Chi Phi fraternity drugged and sexually assaulted her in 2024."She's received multiple threats," Giuffra said on CNN's "State of the Union". He said he too had been threatened.Giuffra said the threats were an attempt to protect the status quo surrounding the case. "I'm not afraid of these people," he said, while describing those behind the threats as people trying to prevent scrutiny of what happened.The allegations have triggered renewed scrutiny of Cornell's handling of the case, as well as the actions of local prosecutors who initially did not pursue criminal charges. The woman filed the civil lawsuit in September against seven fraternity members, Cornell University, the Chi Phi fraternity and other defendants.The case dates back to October 2024, when Jane Doe, then a Cornell student, alleged that she was given alcohol, marijuana and ketamine at the Chi Phi fraternity house before being sexually assaulted after becoming incapacitated. The accused men have denied wrongdoing, with some saying the sexual activity was consensual.New York AG takes over Cornell rape investigationThe handling of the allegations has come under fresh scrutiny after reports revealed discrepancies between the woman's detailed account to campus police and the shorter sworn statement that was provided to prosecutors.In one interview with police, she reportedly told investigators that she was certain she had been raped, but that assertion was not included in the statement sent to prosecutors.Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten had initially declined to pursue charges in 2024. After the civil lawsuit triggered renewed attention, he reopened the criminal investigation and said his office would present evidence to a grand jury for possible indictment.However, New York Governor Kathy Hochul later said she had "lost faith" in the Tompkins County DA's ability to fairly oversee the case. She appointed state Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor, meaning James' office will now oversee the criminal investigation.Hochul has also criticised the initial handling of the allegations by Cornell police and local prosecutors, saying the woman had been failed by institutions that were supposed to protect her.Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff said on Saturday that the university would review the role of fraternities and sororities on campus following the public outcry. He said such organisations could provide students with friendship and community, but "being part of a group can never diminish individual responsibility."US President Donald Trump has criticised the decision to appoint James, saying the people she investigates would not get a "fair shake". Giuffra, however, said the case should not be turned into a political issue."It has nothing to do with politics," he said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 1987, Mississippi rebuilt 1.5 miles of State Route 15 with pond ash from a coal plant; after three years, its stronger ash sections bent far less than the ordinary control road
articles.summary: Discover how Mississippi utilized coal ash to rebuild State Route 15 in 1987, showcasing its impact on road durability and performance over three years.
articles.body: Mississippi rebuilt about 1.5 miles of State Route 15 in Stone County in 1987 by using pond ash from subbituminous coal. The project divided the roadway into five test sections, with four using lime-stabilized ash and one using cement-stabilized ash, while a separate 0.85-mile section used mechanically stabilized sand-clay material as the control. Engineers used the sections to compare the performance of different ash mixtures with the control section, and the road was monitored after construction, with measurements taken over the following three years to assess pavement condition and deflection.Five test sections on one roadPond ash is a mixture of ash materials collected and stored in settling ponds at coal-fired power plants, and the project was designed to examine pond ash as a base material for a paved road. The five test sections used different stabilization mixes, with four containing lime at concentrations that ranged from 2% to 7%, and one using 7.5% Portland cement. The control section used mechanically stabilized sand-clay subbase material.All of the sections were mixed in place, and a double bituminous surface treatment was then applied as the road's wearing surface. The Federal Highway Administration recorded the project in its User Guidelines for Waste and Byproduct Materials in Pavement Construction, and lists the Mississippi project as an example of a stabilized road base using Class C pond ash.Engineers measured how the road movedThe roadway was monitored after construction, and deflection measurements were taken every year through 1990. Deflection is the amount a pavement surface moves under a load, and engineers use the measurement to assess how a pavement responds when traffic places a load on it. The FHWA record says that the sections that contained 6% and 7% lime, along with the 7.5% cement section, recorded much lower deflection readings than the control section and the section containing only 2% lime.It did not mean that every ash mixture performed identically, since the type and amount of stabilizing material mattered. The control section and the 2% lime section had no observed cracking after three years, while the cement-stabilized section had the most cracking. The FHWA classified the cracking as shrinkage-related rather than structural, and noted that shrinkage cracking is common in cement-stabilized granular materials, particularly soil-cement mixtures.Three years of field dataA separate Federal Highway Administration record of the Mississippi project describes the work as an evaluation of power plant pond ash for highway construction. The study tracked the test sections for three years and included measurements of pavement deflection, visible distress, ride quality, and the strength of material cores. The project report says that both the test sections and the control section provided good performance during the three-year service period.The results provided highway engineers with field data on several different ash mixtures rather than a single yes-or-no test. The control section provided a conventional comparison, while the stabilized ash sections showed how changes in lime and cement content affected pavement behavior. The FHWA's later guidance lists the Mississippi project among documented applications of coal ash in stabilized road bases.The Route 15 project was built as a field test, but the road was still a working state highway, and by 1990, engineers had three years of measurements from sections built with pond ash and from the conventional control section. The records show lower deflection in the stronger stabilized ash sections, while the observed cracking remained nonstructural, and the project became one of the documented U.S. examples of coal combustion material being used in highway pavement construction.You use AI every day. articles.title: Indian police accused of sexual harassment against journalists at protest
articles.summary: The allegations were made after police detained dozens of protesters demanding the resignation of the election chief over changes to voter rolls.
articles.body:
Three female journalists have accused police officers in India of sexual harassment during street protests in the capital Delhi.

The claims were made on Saturday after the force detained scores of young people calling for the resignation of the chief election commissioner.

In a post on social media, Delhi Police said its New Delhi District had received the complaint, and it had been transferred to its crime branch for a "fair and impartial" inquiry.

Thousands of protesters gathered in Delhi and Mumbai cities for a third day on Sunday demanding that Gyanesh Kumar step down over large-scale changes to voter rolls.

The Election Commission says the exercise is intended to remove duplicate and ineligible entries - and so far, 130 million names have been struck off the voters' list.

Videos online show people being physically dragged away from the Jantar Mantar protest site in central Delhi.

The accusations by the women journalists include inappropriate touching by some police.

Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi said women fear for their safety and the home ministry must "answer for this".

"Police dragged me by my hair," Aahna Singh, an activist and student at Jawaharlal Nehru University told Reuters news agency during the protests.

She said the police were resorting to "brutality".

The Press Club of India has demanded immediate action on the complaints against police officers, saying it was "shocked and dismayed" by the treatment of journalists.

"Behaviour of this kind cannot be normalised in a democracy. Journalists must be allowed to work freely, without fear, and document those who gather to raise various issues," it said in a statement.

The protesters say the voter-roll revision will benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

The Election Commission says the exercise is intended to remove duplicate and ineligible entries.

It says the last revision was done nearly a quarter of a century ago and the voters' list needs to be updated to account for those who have died, left the country or are registered in more than one place as they've moved to a new address.

But the exercise has been mired in controversy from the start with the opposition parties accusing Kumar of manipulating voters' list to favour the BJP during elections. Both the BJP and the Election Commission have rejected the accusations.

The protesters have included supporters of the influential Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) that began as an online satirical movement.

The pressure group recorded its first major victory in July when it forced the then Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign after weeks of protests calling for education reforms.

The CJP called for the latest protest after a report in The Indian Express said that Kumar's two fellow election commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had formally objected at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders they said had been issued without their knowledge.

The differences were reported to be mostly over the controversial revision of the country's electoral rolls known as the Special Intensive Revision, or SIR, which began last year.

The Election Commission has defended its way of working and said in a statement that "differing views" were part of the "decision-making process" and that all the decisions were taken unanimously.

But the revelations sparked a furore, with opposition leaders demanding Kumar's resignation.

articles.title: Heated discussions on Barrow town centre's future
articles.summary: A consultation is held on plans for Barrow town centre, after its theatre and market was closed.
articles.body:
Heated discussions between the public and bosses were had at a consultation on the future of a town.

A first look at plans to regenerate Barrow town centre were unveiled this week at consultation events, including ideas for a new theatre and cultural quarter .

Questions were asked about the Forum theatre venue and Barrow Market, which closed suddenly in 2023 over asbestos issues, and ranged from scrutiny of the decision to demolish them to asking when a replacement would come.

Westmorland and Furness Council's director of planning, regeneration and communities, Gareth Candlin, said a theatre was one of the authority's "ambitions" but it had to be economically viable.

One resident, who did not want to be named, told the Local Democracy Reporting Service : "I've lived in Barrow all of my life, I work in the shipyard and am really passionate about the potential the town has.

"There is a lot of talk about the investment but we haven't actually seen any of it turn into anything.

"Barrow has a reputation elsewhere for being a bit of a dead-end town, but I really like living here."

She added the likes of BAE pay well, so workers "have money to spend" but asked "where can you spend it" in town.

Barrow town centre is undergoing a £200m regeneration, with the town getting £20m a year from 2025.

The funding from central government is the responsibility of Team Barrow - a partnership between government, BAE Systems and the Liberal Democrat-led council.

In August, £23m was announced for a first phrase which would address the closure of the theatre and market, including a market village, a "temporary event space" and a programme of arts, culture and entertainment.

Candlin said theatre builds in recent years had cost between £50m and £60m.

He said: "If we do build it, we don't want to spend £50m and then it shuts its doors three years down the line because it runs out of money."

The temporary theatre was expected to come in 2028, Candlin added.

articles.title: Trump-linked drone firm’s Pakistan deal raises questions over US arms thaw
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: An obscure American defence start-up has suddenly acquired an outsized geopolitical significance after signing a
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: An obscure American defence start-up has suddenly acquired an outsized geopolitical significance after signing a memorandum of understanding with the Pakistan army and securing an initial order for unmanned aerial systems, raising questions in Indian strategic circles over whether the deal could be an indicator of a wider reopening of US military supplies to Pakistan.Powerus, a Florida-based company barely a year old, signed the agreement during a September visit to Pakistan led by its president and co-founder Brett Velicovich, a former US army special operations intelligence analyst. The company says the initial order is limited, but Velicovich has said its longer-term ambition is to combine American and Pakistani technology and potentially establish manufacturing in Pakistan.“Powerus has received a limited procurement order from the ministry of defence of Pakistan for unmanned aerial systems and associated support. The order represents an expansion of our international defense business. We have also signed a strategic mou. It sets a framework for potential expanded cooperation in unmanned and autonomous systems, subject to definitive agreements and government approvals,” the company said in a September 17 announcement.“We are proud to support Pakistan’s Ministry of Defence, and the memorandum gives both sides a strategic framework to build upon.” Velicovich added.The Pakistan deal is particularly notable because Powerus has access to Ukrainian defence technology developed during the war with Russia. In March, it established Powerus USA, in partnership with Wyoming-based G1 Exploration, to commercialise Ukrainian autonomous defence systems. Powerus owns 51% of the venture, while G1 contributed intellectual property covering seven fully developed products and other systems under development.aThe partnership produced the Guardian family of counter-drone interceptors, designed to destroy hostile unmanned aircraft. Powerus says Guardian has been developed with Ukrainian technology and battlefield experience, which have received rave notices in the US. This creates an unusual – and in Indian eyes an unprecedented – chain: Ukrainian drone technology, brought into a US defence company, is now potentially being transferred to Pakistan, a country whose military has been rapidly expanding its own drone capabilities.The political sensitivity is heightened by Powerus's links to the Trump family. Powerus completed its merger with Nasdaq-listed Aureus Greenway Holdings on October 1 and now trades as Powerus Corporation under the symbol PUSA. Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump are reported to be investors in Aureus through American Ventures; regulatory filings have indicated an indirect stake of about 9.9% in the combined company.Ironically, the deal has also caused unease in some Pakistani circles because of Powerus’ Israeli links, with one of its co-founders reported to be former IDF officer Ziv Marom. Some analysts are questioning why Pakistan, which already builds its own drones and buys others from China and Turkiye, a company that was founded only last year and sells drones to India too. Others view it as Pakistan -- which is heavily dependent on China for major weapons imports -- diversifying its suppliers.Indeed, the most intriguing aspect of the Pakistan deal is that Powerus had already entered the Indian defence market. In June, Powerus subsidiary Tandem Defense was reported to have granted Mumbai-based Paras Defence and Space Technologies exclusive licence to manufacture and commercialise the Guardian-1 counter-drone interceptor in India. So effectively, the same American company is now pursuing defence cooperation with both India and Pakistan, which fought a short war in May 2025 in which drones played a prominent role.The juxtaposition is attracting close attention in military circles in India, which has invested heavily in its strategic relationship with Washington and is viewing the transfer of advanced unmanned technology to Pakistan with concern. Of course, the US has a long history of supplying arms to rival states, and the Powerus arrangements do not by themselves demonstrate a change in policy towards India.The larger question though is whether Powerus represents something more consequential: a gradual restoration of the US-Pakistan defence relationship -- which has largely been in ice over the past two decades -- in a capital where institutional and congressional oversight is perceived to have broken down with opportunists having a free run.The Trump administration itself began loosening controls last December when it approved a $686 million package to modernise Pakistan's existing F-16 fleet. The consignment included 92 Link-16 tactical data systems, cryptographic equipment, avionics, training and logistical support. The stated US rationale was “to preserve Pakistan's interoperability with US and partner forces and support counterterrorism and future contingencies.”Powerus could empower the Pakistani military even more. Drones, counter-drone systems, communications, surveillance and electronic warfare are less politically conspicuous than supplying Pakistan with new fighter aircraft or major offensive weapons, but they are also the technologies whose importance has been demonstrated by the wars in Ukraine and the India-Pakistan conflict.

articles.title: Christa Pike’s lawyer says she has not regained consciousness since her failed Tennessee execution
articles.summary: Christa Pike has remained unconscious and on a ventilator at a hospital in the four days since her failed execution in Tennessee, and her prognosis might not be known for days more, one of her lawyers said Sunday.
articles.body: Christa Pike has remained unconscious and on a ventilator at a hospital in the four days since her failed execution in Tennessee, and her prognosis might not be known for days more, one of her lawyers said Sunday. Little has been released about Pike’s condition since Wednesday night’s execution attempt. She has since remained hospitalized under guard as doctors try to get the massive dose of the barbiturate pentobarbital out of her system. When asked whether she ever regained consciousness after the execution attempt, Assistant Federal Defender Stephen Ferrell, Pike’s lawyer, said on CNN’s “State of the Union”: “Not that I am aware of.” Lawyer says Pike’s medical decisions are being decided by someone else Pike, now 50, was 18 when she and her boyfriend tortured and killed a classmate, Colleen Slemmer, in a jealous rage in 1995. She became one of the youngest women to be sent to death row. Tennessee prison officials gave Pike two doses of the lethal injection drug on Wednesday night. The pentobarbital didn’t kill her, but her lawyers said her arms were burned and blistered from the caustic drugs. Pike gave someone her medical power of attorney and that person is protecting her privacy, Ferrell said. “I’m not sure what all they may have told that person,” Ferrell said. Pike’s attorneys have not identified who is making Pike’s medical decisions. They said they may not know for several more days whether or not she can recover. “We don’t know right now, and we may never know what sort of torture she endured during that process, where her consciousness was, what physical pain there was — what mental torture she went through,” Ferrell said. A spokeswoman for Pike’s defense team said in a statement early Sunday that “we appreciate all respect for Christa’s rightful privacy.” Pike’s lawyer says Tennessee needs to be more open about executions Pike’s execution was delayed for more than eight hours Wednesday as the U.S. Supreme Court considered, and ultimately overturned, a federal appeals court ruling to halt her lethal injection so judges could thoroughly review whether the jury that sentenced her to death should have considered sexual abuse she said she suffered as a child. Her attorneys asked a court Friday to order Tennessee prison officials to preserve any written records, communication, images or video from the execution. Tennessee, like many other states with capital punishment, keeps many details about executions secret from the people involved to details about how the drugs are manufactured or obtained or any tests done on their quality. “The state of Tennessee has got to start telling its people exactly what it is doing so that in the democratic process, the people of Tennessee can decide if that’s what they want to be done in their name,” Ferrell told CNN. Tennessee has struggled with executions before This was the second time this year Tennessee has not been able to execute a prisoner who was seemingly moments away from death. In May, Tennessee stopped the execution of Tony Carruthers after staff placed an IV into his right arm but couldn’t get a secondary IV line. Commissioner of the Tennessee Department of Correction Frank Strada announced Saturday he was resigning. Gov. Bill Lee has ordered an independent investigation into the state’s capital punishment system conducted by former U.S. Attorney Ed Stanton. He also reviewed Tennessee’s execution procedures after Lee called off a different execution in 2022 and found the state did not comply with its own lethal injection process. Prison officials and the Tennessee Attorney General’s Office have said little since Pike was taken to the hospital. Future of Pike’s death penalty case is unclear If Pike recovers, it is unclear what will happen in her death penalty case. Pike’s lawyers have asked the governor to commute her punishment to a life sentence. Pike didn’t deny she killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in 1995. The two were classmates at Knoxville Job Corps. Prosecutors said Pike feared Slemmer was a romantic rival and lured her to a secluded area where she and her boyfriend slashed Slemmer with a box cutter and beat her with a large chunk of asphalt. The case got widespread attention because of the brutality of the killing, the ages of the people involved and because a satanic symbol was carved into the victim’s body.

articles.title: Christa Pike's prognosis still unclear after failed execution, lawyer says
articles.summary: Pike's lawyer says doctors are still trying to clear two lethal doses of pentobarbital from her body.
articles.body:
US murderer Christa Pike remains critically ill in hospital and her prognosis is still unclear following her failed execution, her lawyer has said on Sunday.

Speaking to CNN on Sunday morning, Pike's lawyer Stephen Ferrell said doctors were still trying to clear two doses of pentobarbital from her body.

Pike, 50, was sentenced to death following her conviction for murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995.

She survived two execution attempts on Wednesday, and was transferred to a hospital in Nashville, Tennessee.

Ferrell said: "She's still in the hospital, on a ventilator, critically ill, we really don't know the prognosis yet, and may not know for several days."

He didn't believe she had regained consciousness at any point, adding that he has been receiving updates through her medical power of attorney rather than consulting directly with doctors.

He has not been in to see her. "She is guarded. I'm not sure who may have seen her," he said.

Authorities have not yet said whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have also not offered an explanation for what went wrong. But Tennessee Governor Bill Lee suspended all executions for the rest of the year - and the head of prisons in the state said he would resign on Saturday.

"If she recovers - she may not fully recover - and there may be issues about her competence. I mean, we just don't know any of this," Ferrell said. "We have had no discussions about this. The Tennessee attorney general's office so far has not given us any indications of what their intentions will be."

I interviewed Christa Pike 20 years ago - I can't stop thinking about her

He called on the governor to commute her death sentence to a life sentence "at the very least". "She has endured a torturous attempt at executing her," he said. "She's spent over 30 years in prison, most of that in solitary confinement."

"We don't know right now - and we may never know - what sort of torture she endured during [her failed execution]."

Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer in 1995.

She was sentenced to death the following year after a media frenzy around the killing in Knoxville, Tennessee.

Slemmer's mother May Martinez travelled to Nashville for the execution, which moved ahead despite last-minute legal challenges.

Martinez, who supported Pike's death sentence, told local news outlet WJXX that she "broke down in tears" after finding out it was not successful.

"I think that the state owes me a big apology," she said.

The state's Department of Correction has defended the use of lethal injections, saying "the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out".

Pike's lawyers previously warned that her medical history and anatomy - including thrombocytosis (a blood-clotting condition) and small veins - meant there was a risk she would experience "unnecessary" pain and suffering during a lethal injection.

articles.title: A Yorkshire farmer turned his 3,000-tonne potato store into a padel club; the new business was fully booked within months
articles.summary: A North Yorkshire farmer has found a new use for a potato store after disappointing returns from the crop prompted him to rethink part of his farming
articles.body: A North Yorkshire farmer has found a new use for a potato store after disappointing returns from the crop prompted him to rethink part of his farming business. Callum Stark converted a 3,000-tonne potato storage building at Fridlington Farms near Sutton-on-the-Forest into two indoor padel courts. His new venture, The Padel Farm, opened in 2025 and quickly attracted strong demand. Within months, the courts were fully booked, turning a space once used for storing potatoes into a new source of income while Stark continues to run the family farm.How a 3,000-tonne potato store became a padel clubThe idea began with a problem familiar to many farmers. The numbers behind a crop were no longer making enough sense. According to Farmers Guardian, Stark lost £12,000 on a potato contract, prompting him to consider how the farm could make better use of its existing assets.The farm covers about 3,000 acres near Sutton-on-the-Forest, and farming remains a central part of the business. But Farm Business Innovation reported that Stark felt the potatoes were not providing enough reward for the level of risk and effort involved.Instead of abandoning agriculture, he looked at what was already available on the farm. One of the largest buildings was a potato store, and that empty space offered an opportunity for something completely different.The answer was padel, a racket sport played on a smaller enclosed court and combining elements of tennis and squash. The Padel Paper described the project as a move that brought two indoor courts, coaching facilities and a coffee shop onto the farm.Why did Stark choose padel for the unused spaceThe choice was closely linked to the sport's growing popularity. Farm Business Innovation reported that there were only around 800 padel courts in the UK at the time, compared with about 33,000 in Spain. For Stark, the shortage of facilities in the UK made the sport an interesting option for a large building that was no longer being used in the same way.The location also gave the project a particular advantage. The Padel Farm is around 15 minutes from York city centre, according to The Padel Paper, while the club's own website describes it as York's first indoor padel and social club.The decision was not simply about putting courts inside a shed. The project was developed with Barney Spratt and Dan Hall alongside Stark, with the aim of creating a place where people could play, socialise and spend time in the countryside.The Padel Paper reported that the team had been inspired by a visit to Blazing Padels near Norwich, where two padel courts had also been installed inside a converted barn.Opening of the Padel FarmThe venue opened in March 2025 at Fridlington Farms, with free introductory sessions for adults and children. The Padel Paper reported that junior activities were planned from the beginning, including a Saturday morning children's club and ladies' taster sessions with free coffee.The early response was strong. Farm Business Innovation later reported that The Padel Farm was fully booked, with courts operating every day from 7am to 11pm. The club's own website now describes the venue as having two indoor courts and opening seven days a week. It says the facility has attracted about 3,000 active members, showing how quickly the project has developed from an experiment in an old agricultural building into an established local sports venue.Development of the converted farm buildingThe Padel Farm has retained elements of its agricultural setting instead of trying to hide its origins. When it opened, The Padel Paper noted features including a coffee bar made from a converted horse box, outdoor seating and the two panoramic courts inside the barn.The project has also been planned as something larger than a pair of courts. In its May 2026 feature, The Padel Paper reported plans for more indoor courts, an outdoor court, a café and bar, wellness areas, spin and Pilates studios, hot tubs and ice baths, alongside a Hyrox gym.For Stark, the transformation also demonstrated the potential sitting inside buildings that farmers may already own. Farm Business Innovation reported that the cost of installing two courts was roughly comparable with buying a destoner for potato farming, while the courts were expected to pay for themselves within a year.Importance of this change for the wider farm businessThe conversion has not replaced farming. Stark still manages the agricultural operation, but padel has added another income stream to the business.Farmers Guardian reports that the project had created a completely new income stream within 3 months, while the same report noted that the wider family farm faces significant financial pressures, including planning for a potential multi-million-pound inheritance tax liability.The experience has become an example of farm diversification based on an asset that was already there. The Padel Paper's 2026 feature described the farm's finances as having faced tight margins, while the new venture was bringing additional visitors and revenue. Potatoes are still grown on the farm, but part of the property now has a very different rhythm, with players arriving throughout the day instead of potatoes being stored inside.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2020, an abandoned Swiss cocoa silo began its second life with studios, a hostel and a restaurant, putting 42 old concrete tubes back to use
articles.summary: Discover how the abandoned cocoa silo in Basel, Switzerland, transformed into Silo Erlenmatt, featuring studios, a hostel, and a restaurant while preserving its historic charm.
articles.body: The silo stood vacant for years before the redevelopment of the surrounding district created an opportunity for a new use. One of them was treated differently in Basel, Switzerland. In the Kleinbasel neighbourhood of the city, a former grain and cocoa silo reopened as Silo Erlenmatt in 2020. Today, it has studios for creative professionals, a café, a conference area, and a hostel. The ingenious element is that visitors sleep and work inside the skeleton of a warehouse that had stored cocoa beans because the historic concrete storage chambers were left in place rather than demolished.The silo stood vacant for years before the redevelopment of the surrounding district created an opportunity for a new use. The Basel foundation Stiftung Habitat, which owns the site, says it understood the historical relevance and the quality of the reinforced concrete frame and opted for a cautious adaptation rather than demolishing it.A silo built for beansThe structure dates back to 1912, when the Basel warehouse business Basler Lagerhausgesellschaft built it on the grounds of the former German freight yard. Grain and cocoa beans were delivered by rail from Rotterdam, stored in the silo and then sent out again to be distributed throughout Switzerland, as the architecture magazine Bauwelt said in its 2022 report on the project. Behind the slightly classical-looking shell was a grid of 40 square silo chambers arranged in four rows of 10. Each chamber tapered into two hoppers at the bottom. Bauwelt reported that the 20 silos could hold about 3,000 wagonloads of grain, with each load weighing 10 tons.The building was also among Switzerland’s early steel-reinforced concrete structures, a point noted by the project’s engineering and heritage sources. Then the railway stopped running. The yard, which closed in 2003 after 98 years of freight operations, fell into disuse, and the 19 hectares around the silo gradually became one of Basel’s largest redevelopment sites, with houses clustered around a central park. The silo, formerly a free-standing landmark, was now just one in a row of buildings along Signalstrasse, next to a student accommodation and a house for artists. There were certain intractable practical issues in turning a storage building into a place where people might sleep, eat and work.Working with the concreteThe concrete frame couldn’t take the weight of its new task, and the site is directly next to a freeway which the design publication detail identifies as one of the noisiest properties in Switzerland. The architects aimed to stay as close as possible to the existing structure. The silo chambers were retained because they provided a familiar scale for the building's new functions, while only two new floor slabs and distribution cores were needed to make the conversion work. Ventilation, brightness and views are now provided by round, port-hole style windows that do not disrupt the historic appearance of the front.Some of the job was physically stubborn. Diamond saws were used to carve the round apertures through the thick concrete, according to Bauwelt. Only the outermost rows of cells at the northern and southern ends were removed, and those areas now carry the escape routes, earthquake strengthening and bracing that made it possible to maintain the remainder. Concrete filled several of the hoppers to steady the building should the ground shake. Basel Tourism defines the building as having concrete bridges with bare black steel railings that traverse empty silo chambers on the top floors to access the rooms and studios. The project received several architecture awards, including Best Architects 21, Beton 21, the Building Award 2021, the Prix AMO 2023 and the Gutes Bauen 2023 distinction from the cantons of Basel-Landschaft and Basel-Stadt.Inside the silo todayThe completed facility, according to Stiftung Habitat, is a hostel with 20 rooms and 60 beds, a conference room and studios. The Silo Design and Boutique Hostel, operated by the Basel hospitality business Krafft Gruppe, has four-bed dorms as well as double rooms, and the studios are on the courtyard side, away from the road. The initial brief called for a café on the ground floor opening into a public courtyard with outdoor seating, and the hostel’s website now says that level is a Living Room providing breakfast, coffee and snacks to guests and anybody who goes in.Part of the idea was affordability. Bauwelt reported in 2022 that a bed in a four-person dorm cost 42 Swiss francs, while a deluxe double room cost 125 francs. The environment is part of the charm. The larger Erlenmatt Ost district is located next to a metropolitan freeway with more than 100,000 vehicles a day, but the Stiftung Habitat says the neighbourhood’s own energy centre supplies it with 100% renewable energy, with solar panels on every roof.For anyone planning a visit, Silo Erlenmatt stands at Signalstrasse 37 in Basel, within walking distance of the Badischer Bahnhof station. A 1912 cocoa store that could easily have been flattened now holds beds, desks and coffee cups, and the concrete chambers that once held beans are still the first thing a visitor notices.You use AI every day. articles.title: Jeffrey Archer returns to his former Wellington School library
articles.summary: The author visits Wellington School ahead of the publication of his final book of his career.
articles.body:
Bestselling author Jeffrey Archer has returned to his former school ahead of the publication of his final book.

Archer, who is 86 years old, sold more than 300 million books in his five-decade writing career, including the Clifton Chronicles and Kane and Abel, and has often set the novels in his home town of Wellington, Somerset.

His last book, Adam and Eve, is out soon, and Archer took the opportunity to visit his former school library at Wellington School.

"It's wonderful to come back. What I got a real thrill about when I was walking towards the library is seeing the young boys and girls and thinking, 'that's the next generation'," Archer said.

"The library is really special to me because it brings back so many happy memories," Archer added.

"I was on a scholarship because we had no money, I came from Weston-super-Mare and we had no money. I would never have got in without a scholarship."

Juliet Handley, development officer at Wellington School, said: "He's got so much energy and enthusiasm. It's wonderful to see.

"He was an incredible gymnast; he played our corps of drums. We are one of the only schools in the country that still have a corps of drums. It's lovely to see it's a tradition that lives on."

Handley added that she feels lucky to work with the older Wellington School alumni.

"I constantly hear that the school inspired them to do what they ended up doing, whether it's geography, business or in Jeffrey's case, writing books that sold worldwide," she said.

"To have such a big career, you have to have a passionate desire to do it; you won't keep going otherwise.

"He wrote 18 drafts for this book he's just publishing by hand. You've got to have a love for it."

Archer's last book is a love story about a young couple called Adam and Eve, set against Hitler's dilemma about whether or not to invade Britain.

He said: "I had to write it so smoothly that you believe that these two people changed the history of the world.

"I was born in 1940, so the first five years of my life we were in war. I remember people with one arm, one leg, blind; that was common for me."

When asked why he decided it would be his last book, he said: "I think everybody would like to run their last 100 metres at the Olympics and win the gold medal. I think the clever thing about life is to know when to get out."

articles.title: Mass protests demanding poll chief resignation shake India for third day
articles.summary: Protesters say the election commission’s voter-roll revision has removed millions of eligible voters to benefit PM Modi.
articles.body:
Thousands of youth and opposition protesters have rallied for a third day in India demanding the resignation of the country’s election commission chief.

Thousands marched in Mumbai on Sunday, while others gathered for a third day of demonstrations in New Delhi. The protests began on Friday demanding that Election Commission of India (ECI) chief Gyanesh Kumar step down due to reports that he has overseen voter-roll revisions removing millions from electoral lists.

Protesters say the disenfranchisement stands to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Both the ECI and the BJP have denied the allegations.

Led by opposition leaders Raj Thackeray and Uddhav Thackeray, thousands marched in Mumbai on Sunday, waving Indian flags and calling for Kumar to step down.

In the capital, New Delhi, protesters started gathering in the early evening. As on previous days, some were detained by police as they arrived, according to the Reuters news agency.

Police in the capital have clamped down in a bid to prevent protesters from assembling over the last two days, detaining dozens and taking them away by bus.

Some of the detainees were released later on Friday and Saturday, but police registered cases against some on charges of violating orders banning mass gatherings in the centre of the capital.

“⁠I just want to tell the ruling party this much … We are angry about how you are wielding that power. ⁠It’s the people of this country who should decide who sits in power and who sits in opposition, not the election commission,” Raj Thackeray told the crowd in Mumbai.

The ECI says the voter-roll revision is designed to remove duplicate, deceased or ineligible entries and maintain electoral integrity. On Friday, it directed its officials to register eligible voters inadvertently omitted from electoral rolls.

Kumar has not publicly responded to the demands for his resignation or commented on the protests, which look set to continue over the coming days, with more rallies planned.

An alliance of India’s opposition parties plans to launch protests to “save democracy” with a march to the election commission office on Tuesday. The Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has announced plans for a major rally in New Delhi on October 10.

“Mumbai is out on the streets again for free and fair elections!” Abhijeet Dipke, chief of the CJP, said in a social media post on Sunday.

“Solidarity with all the protesters,” he added. “All Indians need to come together. It’s now or never!”
