articles.title: In 2001, Texas finished a five-year study of six crushed-fly-ash road sections; inspections, core strength and deflection tests found the pavements had performed well
articles.summary: A five-year study by the Texas Transportation Institute demonstrates the effective use of crushed fly ash as a road base, revealing strong performance under real traffic and weather conditions.
articles.body: The Texas Transportation Institute completed a five-year research project on six test pavements in the Atlanta District, submitting its final report in October 2001. Crushed fly ash, a byproduct of coal-fired power plants, served as the base for all of the pavements in the Atlanta District of northeast Texas. The conclusion was clear: the test pavements had done well based on visual surveys, deflection data, and core strengths.The work was performed for the Texas Department of Transportation under a research project from September 1996 to August 2001. Its title was awkward but correct: durability of surface treatments applied to crushed fly ash and long-term performance of crushed fly ash as a flexible base. What was behind that term was a practical question. Could a waste material from the power sector be used as road aggregate and stand up to actual traffic and real weather?The six pavement sections were built between 1993 and 1995, and the formal research project began in September 1996, with the first annual field evaluation conducted in spring 1997. In its first annual assessment, the Texas Transportation Institute reported that most of the test pavements were performing very well, although two showed minor distress that might have been related to the fly ash base.Crushed fly ash for base roadsThis material is no ordinary fly ash. Engineers employed something called hydrated fly ash, which is formed by curing a Class C fly ash, a self-cementing variety, with moisture. It sets hard and forms a hard, rock-like substance. This material can be fractured to form a synthetic aggregate. If the material is properly handled and compacted at its optimum moisture level, it can still build strength after being placed in the road. TTI’s final report particularly discusses this behaviour and states that the hydrated fly ash forms a stiff substance that may be crushed to make a synthetic aggregate.The Atlanta District created six pavement pieces using the material as a flexible base. Some parts had a fly ash base of approximately 6.5 to 13 inches, depending on the road, with the recycled material beneath the surface treatment or asphalt layers.What was measuredThe researchers evaluated the pavements through visual surveys, falling-weight deflectometer testing and laboratory analysis of pavement cores. Visual surveys recorded cracking, rutting and other surface deterioration, while the deflectometer measured pavement stiffness.Cores drilled out of the pavement were then evaluated in the laboratory for compressive strength. Researchers also employed ground-penetrating radar in parts of the study to look at the structure of the pavement without digging into it. The detailed testing also showed that the six sections were not behaving identically. TTI identified weak and stiff spots within individual pavement sections, and one pavement was considerably stiffer overall than the other five. Researchers observed the fluctuations and realised that the uniformity of the material could affect performance.Later assessments did not see those worries translating into widespread decline. The final assessment spanning the period from spring 1997 to spring 2001 found that the hydrated fly-ash test pavements had fared satisfactorily based on the combined evidence of visual inspection, deflection and core strength.The challenge of bondingThe researchers conducted another Texas Transportation Institute study on surface-treatment bonding. Laboratory testing investigated various prime materials and the degree of curing of the fly-ash base before the asphalt membrane was applied. They determined that the type of prime material was not the main reason for the poor bond and that the degree of curing prior to the surface treatment was more probably responsible. That difference was important because a pavement base could be solid, but the layer on top of it could still fail to connect properly. The problem wasn’t that the fly ash was unusable as a road basis; it proved that construction time and interaction between pavement layers were also critical.The importance of variabilityThe first-year evaluation showed differences in stiffness between sites within the same sections. So the researchers weren’t investigating some general substance that behaved the same everywhere. They were testing a particular processed fly ash in a controlled construction environment. That was also a limit of the 2001 study. The six test sections provided a small sample of pavements that performed well during the monitored period, but the research did not establish how the material would perform over several decades or under every combination of traffic and weather.So what do the results tell us?The Texas results show that a coal waste product, when properly cured, crushed and compacted, may be used as a flexible road base and continues to acquire strength after placement. Visual inspections, deflection tests and core-strength measurements were used to monitor the six test sections in the Atlanta District. The final assessment stated they performed well. The practical lessons are specific to road authorities: test the uniformity of the ash supply, control moisture during compaction, ensure the base is properly cured before applying a surface treatment, and monitor the pavement over several years rather than assuming an early result will continue. The Texas study did not show that other fly-ash bases will behave in the same way. It showed something more specific: when a suitable Class C ash was processed into a synthetic aggregate and used under controlled construction conditions, it could remain a functioning road base through at least five years of field monitoring.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ukraine ready for US-backed talks with Russia: Zelenskyy
articles.summary: Trilateral talks could happen this month in UAE or another US-proposed venue, says the president.
articles.body:
Ukraine is ready to hold trilateral talks with the United States and Russia this month, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said.

The Ukrainian president made the comments on Sunday during a news conference alongside German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Kyiv . He said Ukraine supports a swift timeline for returning to talks to try to end the war fought for over four and a half years.

US efforts to broker a ceasefire have been paused since Washington launched its war on Iran. However, Washington is now pushing for technical-level talks by the end of October, Zelenskyy said.

He confirmed earlier reports that the United Arab Emirates, which has hosted previous talks, could again be the setting for a meeting.

“I confirmed to [the US] that our side is ready to support this timeline,” Zelenskyy said, adding that Kyiv is open to meeting in the UAE or “another country proposed by the American side”.

Washington had also been in touch with Moscow about the plan, Zelenskyy said. The Kremlin said last month that it did not rule out the possibility of three-way talks this month.

Despite suggestions of their willingness to discuss an end to the conflict, both Russia and Ukraine have also said they will ramp up long-range attacks on military and related targets.

Moscow has said it is targeting Ukraine’s energy sector as winter approaches. Last year, similar attacks knocked out power and heating for days on end as temperatures plummeted to minus 20C.

Zelenskyy on Sunday said he was “amazed” by Russia’s “savage desire to escalate the situation every day”.

He yet again accused Moscow of targeting “civilian infrastructure, including data centres and mobile network facilities”.

“Honestly speaking, I am not surprised by this approach to the war – by Russia’s hatred towards Ukraine – but I am surprised by the specific tactics used”, the Ukrainian leader said.

Alongside the return of the US to efforts to broker a ceasefire, India on Sunday said that it aims to step up its efforts to play a larger role in mediating an end to the conflict.

Speaking at the Munich Security Conference in New Delhi, Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar said his country had become more involved in recent months, specifically regarding shipping in the Black Sea, which has been plagued by mines and attacks on commercial vessels .

India was also “going beyond that,” said Jaishankar, including with discussions on grain and energy exports and “on non-attack possibilities,” he said.

articles.title: Zelenskyy claims Putin shared jet-drone technology with North Korea
articles.summary: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Sunday that Russia may have shared technology behind its jet-powered drones with North Korea, deepening
articles.body: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Sunday that Russia may have shared technology behind its jet-powered drones with North Korea, deepening concerns over growing military cooperation between Moscow and Pyongyang.According to news agency Reuters, when asked at a press conference whether Russia had shared its latest jet-drone technology with North Korea, Zelenskyy gave a direct response, “Yes, of course.”“They (Russia) are sharing with North Korea all the technologies. I don't know about the ballistic and etc, but I think, yes, because North Korea helped them with missiles,” he added.The comments come as Russia has intensified its offensive against Ukraine, including a surge in drone attacks on Kyiv. A Russian drone struck the Pivnichnyi Bridge in the Ukrainian capital on Sunday, while Moscow warned it would further step up strikes after Kyiv pledged to target Russian oil refineries. Russia’s defence ministry said its forces would increase attacks on “military and military-industrial facilities, as well as related infrastructure”, as Ukraine’s air defences face mounting pressure.Zelenskyy said Russia and North Korea had expanded weapons cooperation during the full-scale war. North Korea has supplied Russia with artillery shells and ballistic missiles that Moscow has used in attacks on Ukrainian cities, while thousands of North Korean soldiers have been deployed to Russia to gain combat experience.His remarks also came a week after he warned that Moscow was preparing to recruit another 10,000 North Korean military personnel to fight alongside Russian forces against Ukraine.Russia has also sharply increased its use of jet-powered drones in recent weeks. According to the Kyiv Independent, Russia’s Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones can reach speeds of up to 500 and 600 kilometres per hour respectively, making them harder for Ukrainian FPV drones and mobile fire teams to intercept.Ukraine has said the increased deployment of such drones is placing additional pressure on its already strained air-defence network. In some recent attacks on Kyiv, jet-powered drones reportedly accounted for around two-thirds of all drones launched.Zelenskyy said on September 26 that Russia planned to spend $12 billion next year on producing jet-powered drones and loitering munitions.South Korea and Western countries have previously raised concerns that Moscow could be assisting Pyongyang’s weapons development in return for military support for Russia’s war in Ukraine.You use AI every day. articles.title: Carol Vorderman to receive prestigious award at Bafta Cymru 2026
articles.summary: Vorderman was honoured alongside casting director Lauren Evans ahead of the ceremony.
articles.body:
Presenter Carol Vorderman says she feels humbled and excited to receive an award for outstanding contribution at this year's Bafta Cymru, celebrating excellence in film, TV and games.

Vorderman is set to be presented with the Siân Phillips Award while Lauren Evans is taking home an award for her contribution to the film I Swear, which cemented her reputation as one of the leading casting directors in Britain.

Lee Walters, Bafta Cymru chair, said the two women have taken "very different paths", but have both "achieved so much and thoroughly deserve to be celebrated".

The awards will be presented at the ICC Wales, in Newport, where Bafta Cymru has been held since 2024.

Vorderman, from Prestatyn, Denbighshire, began her career on the popular quiz show Countdown where she was the numbers expert and co-presenter for more than two decades.

She said it was one of her proudest achievements and she became a household name across Britain.

The 65-year-old has also chaired a UK government taskforce on maths education and founded an online learning resource designed to build children's confidence.

She has also used her platform to champion accessible education for all and she was awarded an MBE for services to broadcasting in 2000.

Former Doctor Who showrunner Russell T Davies took the Siân Phillips award last year.

Evans, from Hendy, Carmarthenshire, will be awarded the Outstanding Contribution to Craft award after working on a range of productions including Game of Thrones, King Lear and The Danish Girl.

In recent years, she has worked on Sex Education, Lost Boys and I Swear which was nominated for six Bafta awards earlier this year.

Evans ended up winning the award for Best Casting saying she was "incredibly proud" to represent Welsh voices at the 2026 ceremony.

She said she was honoured to be recognised at the Bafta Cymru awards and that she wants to "keep elevating our Welsh creatives and our Welsh talent".

She added: "It's not as much of a closed industry as it was, but there is still so much more work to be done."

The awards consist of 17 categories this year, with actors such as Eve Myles and Matthew Rhys being nominated.

Feature film Madfabulous - which tells the story of an eccentric 19th Century Welsh aristocrat - leads the way at this year's Bafta Cymru awards with six nominations.

It's a Sin actor Callum Scott Howells, who stars as Henry Paget in Madfabulous, previously said it was a "genuine honour" to portray the fifth Marquess of Anglesey.

The full list of Bafta Cymru 2026 nominations can be found here .

Walters congratulated the nominees last month and said "each is a testament to the creativity, skill and dedication of the people working across Wales' screen industries, both in front of and behind the camera".

articles.title: Police investigating Flydubai co-pilot’s Australia ties
articles.summary: Australian police and intelligence join the list of those probing the incident.
articles.body:
Authorities have said they are investigating the links of the co-pilot of the Israel-bound Flydubai flight with Australia.

A multi-agency Australian police and intelligence team – the Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team – is carrying out the probe, a spokesperson said on Sunday.

Mystery surrounds the co-pilot, who is accused of attacking the captain with an axe and attempting to seize control of Flight FZ1073 from Dubai as it approached Israel, and how he was able to acquire his seat in the plane’s cockpit.

He has been identified in media reports as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami .

He had been barred from flying in his own country because of concerns that he had adopted “extremist” views, The Associated Press news agency cited sources as saying.

While al-Hammami reportedly spent part of his life in the United Arab Emirates, the Reuters news agency, citing sources briefed on the Australian investigation, reported that he studied at a university in the Australian city of Melbourne.

A third unnamed source told the agency that he studied at RMIT University, a public research university in Melbourne, about a decade ago.

The Financial Times also reported al-Hammami’s links to Australia. Citing two sources familiar with the Australian investigation, the FT said al-Hammami had allegedly visited what it described as “radical mosques and extremist websites” while in the country.

Disaster was averted after passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot and a reserve pilot took over its controls and completed an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

However, the case has raised questions about security in Israel, which has some of the world’s strictest aviation security measures.

The prosecutor general of the UAE, Hamad Saif al-Shamsi, has labelled the attack an attempted “terrorist act”.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said that Israel has longstanding arrangements with foreign airlines aimed at preventing pilots who are nationals of countries without diplomatic relations with Israel from flying there.

Netanyahu said a “loophole” appears to have allowed the Omani pilot to take part in the Flydubai flight, and that Israel would now strengthen its checks.

The UAE has not yet publicly established a motive or announced whether investigators believe al-Hammami acted alone.

UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash said on Saturday that the latest “terrorist” attack is a new warning that the region’s fight against “extremism” is not over.

articles.title: Girl, 12, fatally shot in US during 'dispute over parking space'
articles.summary: Police in Baltimore have said the young girl was not a target of the shooting but was caught in the crossfire.
articles.body:
A 12-year-old girl was killed in Baltimore over the weekend during an apparent disagreement over a parking space, police in the US city said.

The girl was caught in the crossfire of bullets between two men who police said were allegedly fighting over a parking space in a park where children were playing American football.

In addition to the young girl, another woman was also found with gunshot wounds when police arrived on the scene. Two men also visited area hospitals for injuries related to the shooting, police said.

Police are now searching for at least two suspects, Baltimore Police Commissioner Richard Worley said at a news conference.

"What we know is there was some type of argument between two cowards," Worley said. "They both opened fire on each other. In the crossfire, a 12-year-old little girl, who was probably down there watching football, was shot and killed."

Worley said the girl, who police have not named, was not a target of the shooting.

The girl was pronounced dead in hospital. The other three individuals who were injured have non-life-threatening injuries, Worley said.

The incident happened after 18:00 EDT (23:00 BST) on Saturday.

Authorities are still investigating the shooting and have asked any witnesses to bring information to police.

It remains unclear how many shots were fired, Worley said.

"Two grown men got into an argument, and now a 12-year-old is gone," Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott said at the news conference.

"We never should have to say something like that. What happened out here today is one of the most disgusting things I've ever seen in my life."

articles.title: Terror cells inside foreign airlines 'certainly a possibility,' retired pilot warns
articles.summary: Retired Air Force and Delta Air Lines pilot Buzz Patterson said terror cells could infiltrate foreign airlines after a FlyDubai copilot attacked a captain.
articles.body: The man who once carried the nuclear football for former President Bill Clinton is sounding an alarm on potential terror cells inside foreign airlines after a FlyDubai copilot allegedly attacked the captain of an Israel-bound flight and sent the plane into a death-defying, aeronautics-defying dive. "It’s possible that terror cells can exist inside airline companies – overseas, probably a lot easier than here, but it's certainly a possibility," retired Air Force Lt. Col. Buzz Patterson, a former Delta Air Lines pilot of 16 years, told Fox News Digital on Thursday. "And I think it is something that DOJ needs to take a... really good look at." The warning came after a FlyDubai flight from the United Arab Emirates to Tel Aviv was forced to make an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, after the copilot attacked the captain mid-flight, reportedly with the crash ax. The flight was carrying 174 passengers and eight crew, and investigators are still probing the motive, including possible terrorism or mental health factors – both of which leave Patterson concerned for public safety, if not national security. FORMER ISRAELI PM HAILS ‘HEROISM’ AFTER PASSENGERS HELP THWART ALLEGED COCKPIT ATTACK "If you’ve got somebody that’s, you know, radicalized and if he doesn’t tell his company or his buddies, you’re never gonna know," Patterson said, noting most protocols rely on "self-reporting your activities." "So that's part of the problem, I think, that we're going to start seeing pop up in airline profiles and pilot profiles is we have a lot of people out there that probably shouldn't be flying airplanes." The warning comes amid the revelations that a crash ax found behind the copilot chair in the Boeing 737 was used to bludgeon the pilot in an effort to commandeer the aircraft. "Every 737, and that's what I flew my entire life of all the different models, has a crash ax in the cockpit right behind the copilot so that we can, if we have to, either crack into the door or crack into the windows in the event of an emergency, we can do it," Patterson said. "If the copilot used the crash ax, that is savage because that thing will hurt you." FLYDUBAI PILOT SHOWED WORLD 'THE HIGHEST FORM OF COURAGE,' INDIA'S PM SAYS Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told "FOX & Friends" on Thursday morning that the copilot appeared to have undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination," but said officials would need days to determine whether he had ties to Iran. President Donald Trump since expressed the belief there were ties to Iran. WATCH: PATTERSON CALLS COCKPIT AX ATTACK 'SAVAGE': "International carriers and a few domestic carriers cast a very wide net looking for applicants to be aircrew members and pilots," Patterson said, noting he has emailed Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy of his concerns. "And sometimes that net is a little too wide for who they attract to their airlines." Patterson said U.S. and foreign airlines typically focus heavily on background checks, medical history and aviation violations, but warned that personality changes or radicalization can be difficult to detect once a pilot is hired. Patterson also warned that pilots often fly with colleagues they barely know – much less a deep understanding of their mental health. "You never know what you're gonna bring to the table, what you gonna find in the cockpit next to you when you first get to the cockpit, because we don't fly with the same guys multiple times – we fly with different people almost every single time," he continued. "So every single time we get in a cockpit, we're meeting somebody for the first time, nine times out of 10. "So we never know who we're getting either. And that's why the initial conversation in the cockpit's important. What's your background? What's mine? How's your family life? What's going on in your world? That kind of stuff will flesh out some of that stuff, but you can't flesh it all out. There's just no way. And you don't know." There remains a potential security loophole that needs to be closed with that 737 crash ax in the cockpit, regardless of whether U.S. commercial crews are only randomly screened at airports, according to Patterson. "It's right there," Patterson said Thursday before official reports noted the crash ax as the weapon used by the suspected terrorist. "You know, I can easily see the copilot saying he needed to stretch. He pulls out of the seat because we do this in the 737. It's a very tight cockpit. "Occasionally one pilot will get up, stand in the back of the cockpit and just stretch, you know, get the blood pumping. And it would be very easy for the copilot just to reach down while standing up and grab that ax. I mean, I can see it happening, and God forbid if it did because that's brutal." AMERICA BUILT A FORTRESS AFTER 9/11. THEN THE THREAT STARTED HIDING IN PLAIN SIGHT The terrorist scheme emphasizes that the U.S. should scrutinize not only domestic airline hiring, but also foreign crews entering American airspace, he warned. "I think the United States needs to take a close look at not only who we are allowing to operate heavy machinery in this country, and by heavy machinery, I mean aviation, airplanes," Patterson said. "Who we are hiring and putting into those positions of authority, and then more importantly, who are we allowing from the other carriers to fly into our airspace?" Netanyahu noted to Fox News that the FlyDubai copilot attack was an Omani national who made it through a "loophole" of an Israeli restriction against pilots from countries that do not have diplomatic relations with Israel. While "9/11 changed everything in terms of aviation for everybody," clearly there is far more work to be done to ensure airline safety, he concluded. "Sometimes the guy you're flying with is a wild card and sometimes the guys in the back of the airplane are a wild card. And I think that just some companies do the job, the security job, and they do the vetting screening better than other companies do."

articles.title: Former Chicago mayor Rahm Emanuel declares America is ready for a Jewish president
articles.summary: Former Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel told "Meet the Press" America is ready for a Jewish president as he weighs a 2028 Democratic presidential bid.
articles.body: Former Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel, who is weighing a 2028 Democratic presidential bid, said Sunday on NBC's "Meet the Press" that America is ready to elect its first Jewish president, arguing that voters should be more concerned about Americans losing faith in the country than his own religious beliefs. When moderator Kristen Welker asked whether the country was ready for a Jewish president, Emanuel answered yes before turning the question toward what he described as a broader loss of confidence in America. "My faith is not your problem," he said. "The fact that Americans have lost faith in America, that's our problem. And we should work on that because I've seen a generation of people with an emptiness who've lost faith in America because they think America lost faith with them. That's our problem. It's not my faith." JEWISH HOUSE DEMOCRAT RECALLS COLLEAGUE SAYING THERE IS NO ANTISEMITISM BECAUSE 'ALL THE JEWS ARE RICH' Elizabeth Barcohana, chair of the California Republican Party’s Subcommittee for Jewish Engagement, dismissed Emanuel’s remarks in a Sunday statement to Fox News Digital. "He sounds pathetic," she said. Emanuel, who served as Chicago mayor, a Democratic congressman, White House chief of staff under former President Barack Obama and U.S. ambassador to Japan under former President Joe Biden, has increasingly fueled speculation that he could seek the Democratic nomination in 2028. During Sunday’s interview, he said he would not alter his religious identity for political support and pointed to his record in government as evidence of how his faith influenced him. articles.title: France to close up to 500 schools on Monday over student protests
articles.summary: Lessons will be "totally or partly suspended" in some high schools after clashes between riot police and student protesters, France's education minister says.
articles.body:
Up to 500 schools across France will be partially or totally closed on Monday after clashes between riot police and student protesters in recent days, the French education minister said on Sunday.

Lessons will be "totally or partly suspended" in some "400 to 500" high schools as security conditions "have not been fulfilled", Édouard Geffray said.

He also said 24 schools had been "burned or ransacked" since the start of the protests.

Thousands of students have been demonstrating over education standards and the protests, which started last week, have spread from Paris to other cities, including Montpellier, Nantes and Marseille.

High school pupils and others have objected to a lack of teachers, overcrowded classrooms and run-down buildings.

On Friday, French Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said 735 of France's 3,700 schools had been affected "one way or another" by violent protests.

The education minister warned the number of schools potentially affected on Monday could be comparable to Friday's figure but promised a "partial, progressive return to lessons".

"There are activists - particularly from the far-left - who have infiltrated the high school student movement, hijacked it from the students themselves, and engaged in extreme violence," Édouard Geffray claimed.

"Clearly, this poses a risk to both our staff and our students," he said. Geffray added that 78 staff members in education had been wounded, which he described as "something we have never seen before".

On Friday 1,747 people were arrested, according to French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez.

Riot police clash with students as education protests rage in France

School protests send shivers down French government's spine

Organisers of the protests have called for the demonstrations to continue on Tuesday after accusing the government of a lack of "concrete measures", according to the AFP news agency.

On Sunday, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said his government is taking further steps to "address the difficulties faced by high school students and educational staff".

He said this includes ensuring classes continue, improving facilities, better organising school days and making the French university admissions platform more transparent.

Lecornu also said the government is accelerating the review of its "vandal-pays" bill to ensure that people responsible for damage bear the cost of their actions.

articles.title: 2 dead, dozens injured in mass shooting 2 hours south of Atlanta
articles.summary: Multiple law enforcement agencies responded to a mass shooting from early Sunday morning, leading to two deaths and possibly dozens injured.
articles.body:
Multiple law enforcement agencies responded to a mass shooting from early Sunday morning, leading to two deaths and dozens injured.

Dooly County Coroner Brett Walls told WALB and WMAZ that two people were dead, a 20-year-old man and a 23-year-old man in Vienna, two hours south of Atlanta.

Channel 2 Action News has a reporting team in Vienna to bring you the latest information, LIVE on Channel 2 Action News at 6.

The Georgia Bureau of Investigation confirmed to Channel 2 Action News that they were assisting with response to the incident on Pine Street, working with the Dooly County Sheriff's Office.

Sheriff Craig Peavy told WALB and WMAZ that the Vienna shooting happened during a homecoming celebration from Saturday night and into early Sunday.

Peavy told WMAZ the celebration had about 1,000 people attending and during the festivities, shots were fired at about 50 people.

Police there told WALB that the number of injured was high but could not provide a specific count, at the time.

The sheriff told WMAZ that as many as 25 people were taken to the hospital for treatment of their injuries.

On Sunday morning, the GBI said 35 people were injured.

It is still unclear if any suspects are being sought or in custody, nor is a possible motive for the shooting known.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: To save water, agri varsity seeks ground for groundnut in Punjab
articles.summary: Punjab groundnut farming has fallen 99% since 1968; PAU urges revival to meet winter demand, save 65–70 cm water, and boost incomes with new varieties.
articles.body: Ludhiana: As winter drives demand for groundnuts across Punjab, local markets remain dependent on supplies from Gujarat and Rajasthan, prompting Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) experts to advocate for a major revival of the crop to save water and boost farm incomes.Once a major staple covering 2.2 lakh hectares in 1968, groundnut cultivation in Punjab has collapsed by over 99% to just 1,600 hectares in 2023–24, yielding around 2.8 thousand tonnes with an average output of 7 quintals per acre.PAU extension scientists argue that farmers should capitalise on strong local and out-of-state demand currently met by other states, particularly in historical hubs like Mullanpur and Khanna.“There is a huge demand for groundnut in Punjab and elsewhere, but the demand is largely being met through supplies from other states. If Punjab farmers expand cultivation, they can cater to a market that is already there,” said Dr. Gurpreet Singh, extension scientist (oilseeds), PAU.The university is promoting groundnut as a low-water alternative to water-intensive spring maize, noting that spring groundnut saves 65 to 70 cm of irrigation water, requires significantly less urea, fixes nitrogen to improve soil health, and commands a higher minimum support price (MSP) than paddy.To drive adoption, PAU has recommended high-yield varieties: J 87 (confectionery-grade, yielding 15.3 quintals/acre in spring with 49% oil and high oleic acid), TG 37A (early-maturing), and SG 99 (tolerant to bud necrosis disease).Encouraged by successful trials, farmers in Hoshiarpur, Sangrur, and Kapurthala are expanding cultivation—with one Kapurthala farmer sowing 26 acres of J 87—while PAU has developed a tractor-mounted digger-shaker to solve harvesting labour shortages.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Ludhiana | Silver Rate in Ludhiana | Bank Holidays in Ludhiana | Public Holidays in Ludhiana | Petrol Price in Ludhiana | Diesel Price in Ludhiana | CNG Price in Ludhiana | LPG Price in LudhianaStay updated with the latest Ludhiana news. articles.title: Hardware price surge drives student demand for refurbished laptops
articles.summary: Computer prices surge in Punjab amid global RAM and SSD shortages, pushing students toward refurbished and second-hand laptops as demand outpaces supply.
articles.body: Ludhiana: Soaring component costs have pushed new computers beyond the reach of many students and budget-conscious consumers, fuelling a major market expansion for second-hand and refurbished hardware across Punjab.Industry leaders attribute the sharp increase in laptop and desktop prices to a global shortage of random-access memory (RAM) and solid-state drives (SSDs). Surging demand from the artificial intelligence sector has outpaced manufacturing capacity, driving up wholesale prices for essential hardware.Gurpreet Singh, chairman of the Association of Computer Entrepreneurs (ACE) and the Punjab Association of Computer Traders (PACT), pointed to the growing disparity in retail pricing. “The refurbished computer market is gaining significance because even the base level new laptops are getting out of reach for people,” he said.“The new laptop with a basic 13th-generation processor now costs as much as ₹80,000, machines with 10th-generation processors are available in the range of ₹30,000 to ₹40,000. So parents and students have to resort to refurbished laptops, whereas nearly a year ago, it was possible to get a brand new laptop with the latest specs in this starting range,” Gurpreet Singh said.Explaining the influx of pre-owned devices, Mr. Singh noted that corporate upgrades routinely flood secondary supply chains.“Refurbished laptops are often imported and fixed for any anomalies. Corporate companies change generations with new processors, and their used machines subsequently enter the market. Such laptops are being imported. Because these are available at lower prices, there is good demand for them,” he added.Traders in commercial hubs like Kochar Market report a marked uptick in foot traffic and inquiries. Sahil Sharma, a local second-hand laptop dealer, confirmed the shifting consumer behaviour.“As the prices of laptops have gone up over the past year or so, there have been increased inquiries and purchases of second-hand laptops. This is proving to be beneficial for second-hand and refurbished computer dealers,” Sharma said.Wholesale hardware vendors highlight staggering cost escalations for internal components. Amit Sareen, a computer hardware wholesaler, detailed the market shift.He said that DDR5 RAM from select firms has jumped nearly ten-fold from ₹3,000, while 1TB SSDs that previously sold for ₹5,000 now touch ₹20,000, causing overall PC assembly costs to spiral.Students navigating tight budgets say the price hikes have disrupted academic planning. Navdeep, a local student, noted the difficulty of securing an entry-level machine.“I have been planning to purchase a laptop, but the prices continue to climb. articles.title: Owaisi alleges jail ‘setting’, ‘bail for Rs 2 cr’; prisons dept denies
articles.summary: Owaisi alleges Chanchalguda jail “setting” and bail for Rs 1.5–2 crore; Telangana prisons department rejects claims as baseless, says courts decide bail.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Asaduddin Owaisi, Hyderabad’s member of Parliament, sparked a controversy on Saturday after he accused the Chanchalguda prison superintendent of facilitating illegal activities inside the jail.Speaking at a public meeting in Old City’s Golconda area, Owaisi alleged that a person could secure bail by paying a bribe of Rs 1.5 crore to Rs 2 crore to some jail officials.After a clip of his speech went viral across social media platforms on Sunday, senior prison officials refuted the allegations as baseless.In his speech, Owaisi claimed there was “a complete package” in the jail. “Jail se leke investigating officer tak, jo bolte hain setting kar dena. Allah acha rakhe hamare Chanchalguda ke jail ke superintendent ko. Allah unko ACB se bachale (from the jail authorities to the investigating officer, they say everything can be fixed. May Allah keep the superintendent of our Chanchalguda Jail well; may Allah protect him from the ACB),” alleged Owaisi.He further claimed that the Chanchalguda jail superintendent had permitted a meeting between alleged murder accused inside the prison, where a plot was allegedly hatched to attack AIMIM leaders.“I want to tell those people that AIMIM will not get scared by their actions. It will always support the poor and victims’ families and oppose the murderers,” he said, adding that murder is forbidden in Islam. “We will not give our sons or daughters in marriage to families where any member is a murderer,” he appealed to the Muslims.Reacting to the MP’s statement, D Srinivas, Telangana Prisons deputy inspector general (Hyderabad Range), said the “allegations made against the superintendent are completely baseless, false and without any factual foundation”. “The prison department strongly refutes any allegation of corruption, collusion or extending undue favour to any prisoner,” he said, adding, “The grant of bail is a matter decided by a competent court. articles.title: UK: 2 teenagers jailed for 10 years for arson at Indian restaurant in London
articles.summary: LONDON: Two 17-year-old teenagers have been jailed for 10 years in the UK for an arson attack at an Indian restaurant in London in August last year,
articles.body: LONDON: Two 17-year-old teenagers have been jailed for 10 years in the UK for an arson attack at an Indian restaurant in London in August last year, leaving multiple diners seriously injured.On August 22, 2025, the two, along with a third accomplice, all masked, had stormed the eatery, Indian Aroma, ordering customers to remain in their seats and threatening them with long knives and swords, whilst the third individual emptied canisters of petrol over the furniture, floor, tables and chairs.They then exited the building and held the door mostly shut as one of them lit a taper, which ignited a fireball in front of terrified diners.The court heard how the clothes of one young woman, in her 20s, melted onto her skin and she sustained 50% burns, causing her to be placed in a medically induced coma. Her husband ran out of the restaurant on fire and sustained 51% burns. He told the court he “woke up 45 days after being burnt”.The teenager pair, who denied the charges, were found guilty of arson with intent to endanger life and possession of a bladed article by a jury at the end of a seven-week trial earlier this year. They cannot be named due to their ages.Sentencing them on Friday, Judge Michael Grieve KC said the attack was a sophisticated and professional operation, which involved a “high degree” of planning.“You were both fully aware of the almost inevitable consequences, namely to cause serious harm, up to and including death, to complete strangers. I have no doubt you were carrying out this operation on the direction of some older and more experienced criminal who has not been identified… but you did so with cold blood.”The motive of the attack remains unclear.You use AI every day.
